question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.
All the chefs in the world are famous because of their _____________ skills.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Culinary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Culinary" — relating to cooking or the kitchen.
◦ Example: She has excellent culinary skills and can cook dishes from many cuisines.

• Spelling key: CU + LIN + ARY. The word begins with "Cu-" (as in "cuisine", also connected to cooking) and ends in the common adjective suffix "-ary". Remember it is "culinary", not "kulinary" or "kolinary" — it is never spelt with a "k".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Kulinary" — incorrect; the initial sound is wrongly spelt with a "k" instead of "c".

• Option 2: "Kolinary" — incorrect; both the initial letter and the following vowel are wrong ("ko-" instead of "cu-").

• Option 4: "Colinary" — incorrect; the vowel right after the initial letter is wrong ("co-" instead of "cu-").

NOTE

• Other commonly confused SSC spellings related to food/cooking: cuisine, gourmet, nutritious, vegetarian.

• Remember: words ending in "-ary" are common in English (e.g., necessary, secretary, dictionary, culinary) — always double-check the preceding vowel/consonant cluster, since that is where SSC usually places the trap.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
When I saw him, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. see him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contains a "when clause" referring to a future action, with the main clause "I will ask him to return the book" in the Simple Future Tense.

• Rule — Clauses of Time/Condition: When a sentence has two clauses joined by time/conditional conjunctions like "when", "before", "after", "till", "until", "as soon as", "if", and the main clause is in the Future Tense, the subordinate (time/conditional) clause must be in the Simple Present Tense, never in the Future Tense.
◦ Example: I will call you when he arrives (not "will arrive").

• Applying the rule: since the main clause "I will ask him..." is in the future, the time clause must use the simple present "see", giving "When I see him, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "shall see him" is incorrect because the time clause cannot itself be in the future tense.

• Option 2: "have seen him" is incorrect because the Present Perfect Tense is not used in this time clause; it wrongly suggests the seeing is already completed before the main action.

• Option 3: "had seen him" is incorrect because the Past Perfect Tense is used for an action completed before another past action, which does not fit this future context at all.

NOTE

• This rule is one of the most frequently tested grammar rules in SSC exams — always check whether the sentence has a time/conditional clause before assigning a tense to the main clause.

• Similar conjunctions that trigger this rule: "unless", "in case", "provided that", "as long as".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Paramount
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Supreme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Paramount" means of the highest importance; supreme, chief or pre-eminent. (सर्वोच्च/सर्वाधिक महत्वपूर्ण)
◦ Example: Safety is of paramount importance in this factory.

• Its closest synonym among the options is "Supreme", meaning highest in rank, authority or importance. (सर्वोच्च)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Inferior (निम्न/घटिया): Lower in rank, status or quality — this is an antonym of paramount, not a synonym.

• Option 2: Collateral (सह-, गौण): Existing side by side, additional or secondary; also used for security offered against a loan.

• Option 4: Trivial (तुच्छ/मामूली): Of little value or importance — again close to the opposite of paramount.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "paramount" useful for SSC: "predominant", "foremost", "principal", "cardinal", "utmost".

• Do not confuse "paramount" (most important) with "tantamount" (equivalent to).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Failing to give proper care and attention
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Lax.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lax" means not strict, careless, or failing to give proper care and attention to something. (ढीला/लापरवाह)
◦ Example: The security at the old warehouse was quite lax.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Cautious (सतर्क): Careful to avoid danger or mistakes — the opposite of the required meaning.

• Option 3: Wild (जंगली/उच्छृंखल): Living or growing in a natural, uncontrolled state; unrelated to carelessness in duty.

• Option 4: Provident (दूरदर्शी): Having or showing foresight; making careful provision for the future — again close to the opposite of "lax".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "lax" with "relax" (to rest) or "lack" (absence of something) — a very common SSC spelling/meaning trap.

• Other one-word substitutions on carelessness: "negligent" (careless in duty), "apathetic" (showing no interest).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Brittle
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Resilient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brittle" means hard but liable to break or snap easily; fragile. (भंगुर/नाजुक)
◦ Example: Old, dry twigs become brittle and snap underfoot.

• Its antonym is "Resilient", meaning able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions; tough and flexible rather than easily broken. (लचीला/मजबूत)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Crunchy (करारा): Making a sharp sound when bitten or crushed — describes texture, not toughness, and is not an opposite of brittle.

• Option 3: Delicate (नाज़ुक): Easily damaged or broken — this is actually close in meaning to "brittle", not opposite to it.

• Option 4: Aloof (उदासीन/अलग-थलग): Distant or not friendly/involved — unrelated to physical fragility.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs for "brittle" tested by SSC: brittle × tough, brittle × sturdy, brittle × flexible.

• "Resilient" is also commonly used for people, meaning able to recover quickly from hardship.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
Out of those group members, Rohan is the one who opposes others, no matter what they tell him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. antagonist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "antagonist" is a person who is actively opposed or hostile to someone or something; one who opposes others. (विरोधी)
◦ Example: In the story, the antagonist constantly works against the hero's plans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Agonist (कर्ता): In drama, a person taking part in a contest; in biology, a muscle or substance that produces an action — unrelated to opposition.

• Option 3: Anatomist (शरीर-रचना विशेषज्ञ): A person who studies the structure of the body (anatomy) — a scientific term, unrelated to opposition.

• Option 4: Protagonist (नायक/मुख्य पात्र): The leading or central character in a story, often playing the very opposite role of the antagonist.

NOTE

• Remember the pair "Protagonist" (hero/main character) vs "Antagonist" (villain/opponent) — one of the most frequently confused one-word substitution pairs in SSC exams.

• Related word: "adversary" (an opponent in a contest or conflict).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The letter was being typed by the secretary when the phone rang.
option_1: The secretary will type the letter when the phone rings.
option_2: The secretary types the letter when the phone rings.
option_3: The secretary was typing the letter when the phone rang.
option_4: The secretary is typing the letter when the phone rings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The secretary was typing the letter when the phone rang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The letter was being typed by the secretary when the phone rang" is in the Passive Voice, Past Continuous Tense (was/were + being + V3).

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "by the secretary" becomes the subject "the secretary"; "was being typed" becomes "was typing"; and "the letter" becomes the object. The unchanged time clause "when the phone rang" is carried over as it is.
◦ Active: The secretary was typing the letter when the phone rang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will type ... rings" wrongly converts the sentence into the Simple Future Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "types ... rings" wrongly converts the sentence into the Simple Present Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "is typing ... rings" wrongly converts the sentence into the Present Continuous Tense.

NOTE

• When converting passive to active, always identify the tense first from the auxiliary verbs used (was/were being + V3 = Past Continuous Passive), then apply the matching active structure for that exact tense — never change the tense during conversion.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A dime a dozen
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Something common and not special.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "A dime a dozen" means something that is very common, easily available and therefore not considered special or valuable. (आम बात/सर्वसुलभ)
◦ Example: Smartphones with these features are a dime a dozen these days.

• The expression originates from a time when a dime (a small US coin) could buy a dozen of some common item, implying the item was cheap and plentiful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Variety of amenities — refers to different facilities/comforts, unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

• Option 3: Very wealthy — this is nearly the opposite sense; the idiom is about things being cheap and common, not about wealth.

• Option 4: A fair trade — refers to an equitable exchange or deal, unrelated to commonness.

NOTE

• Other idioms of commonness/abundance often asked in SSC: "Two a penny" (very common, of little value), "Plentiful as blackberries" (abundant), "A drug in the market" (something in excessive, unwanted supply).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Expertise
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Proficiency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Expertise" means a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular field. (विशेषज्ञता/दक्षता)
◦ Example: Her expertise in data analysis helped the team finish the project early.

• Its closest synonym among the options is "Proficiency", meaning a high degree of competence or skill; expertness. (दक्षता)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Ignorance (अज्ञानता): Lack of knowledge or information — the direct opposite of expertise.

• Option 3: Clumsiness (अनाड़ीपन): Awkwardness or lack of skill in movement or action — again nearly opposite in sense.

• Option 4: Lack (अभाव/कमी): Absence or shortage of something — opposite of having expertise.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "expertise" useful for SSC: "mastery", "skill", "competence", "adeptness", "know-how".

• Do not confuse "expertise" (noun, meaning skill) with "expert" (noun/adjective, meaning a skilled person).

question:
In the following sentence, four words are underlined out of which one word is misspelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
I took out a water tumbler(A) for a drink, but found the water in the metal container (B) had frozen so I couldn't quanch (C) my thirst. I ate some biscuits and offered (D) some to Hillary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word at (C), "quanch", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "quench" — to satisfy a thirst, or to put out a fire.
◦ Example: She drank a full glass of water to quench her thirst.

• Spelling key: QU + ENCH. The word follows the common "-ench" pattern (as in "wrench", "bench", "drench"), not "-anch".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "D" — "offered" is correctly spelt; it is the past tense of "offer" (to present something for acceptance).

• Option 3: "B" — "container" is correctly spelt; it means a receptacle or vessel used to hold something.

• Option 4: "A" — "tumbler" is correctly spelt; it means a flat-bottomed drinking glass without a stem or handle.

NOTE

• Other "-ench" words commonly confused in spelling tests: "clench", "trench", "stench", "wrench".

• Always read misspelt-word questions carefully — the error is usually a single substituted or dropped letter (here, "a" wrongly substituted for "e").

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.
(P) an open mind
(Q) seek it with
(O) for personal growth and development
(R) knowledge is a powerful tool
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ROQP.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (R), "knowledge is a powerful tool", is the main clause and forms the logical starting point of the sentence, as it introduces the subject being discussed.

• Part (O), "for personal growth and development", must follow immediately after (R), since it explains the purpose for which knowledge is a powerful tool.

• Part (Q), "seek it with", logically follows (O), as it introduces advice on how to pursue this tool (knowledge), with the pronoun "it" referring back to "knowledge".

• Part (P), "an open mind", completes the sentence as the object of "seek it with", specifying the manner of seeking knowledge.

• Combining them: "Knowledge is a powerful tool for personal growth and development, seek it with an open mind."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PQRO is incorrect because it begins with "an open mind", which has no grammatical or logical connector at the start of the sentence.

• Option 2: ORPQ is incorrect because it places "for personal growth and development" before the subject-verb clause "knowledge is a powerful tool", which breaks the logical flow.

• Option 3: QROP is incorrect because "seek it with" cannot begin the sentence, as the pronoun "it" has no antecedent yet.

NOTE

• In para/sentence-jumble questions, always first locate the independent main clause (usually containing the subject and main verb) to decide the likely starting part, then trace pronouns like "it", "this", "they" back to their antecedents to fix the sequence.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
Solutions to the country's interior problems are still a long way away.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the country's interior.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the word "interior". The correct word here should be "internal".

• Rule — Interior vs Internal: "Interior" refers to the inside part of a physical space or object (e.g., the interior of a house, the interior of a car), whereas "internal" refers to matters, affairs or issues within an organisation, country or system (e.g., internal problems, internal affairs, internal conflict).
◦ Example: The country is facing serious internal problems such as unemployment and inflation.

• Since the sentence talks about the country's problems in an abstract, administrative sense and not about a physical inside space, the correct phrase is "the country's internal problems", not "the country's interior problems".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "problems are still" is grammatically correct; the plural subject "problems" agrees with the plural verb "are".

• Option 2: "a long way away." is correct; this is a standard idiomatic phrase meaning "far from being resolved".

• Option 3: "Solutions to" is correct; "solution to (a problem)" is the standard preposition pairing in English.

NOTE

• Commonly confused word pairs frequently tested by SSC: "interior vs internal", "economic vs economical", "historic vs historical", "sensory vs sensuous".

• Remember: internal = relating to the inside workings/affairs (abstract); interior = the actual physical inside part (concrete).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Success is not a destination, it’s a journey.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Failure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "Success" means the accomplishment of an aim or purpose; achieving a desired outcome. (सफलता)

• Its antonym is "Failure", meaning lack of success; the state of not achieving a desired outcome. (असफलता)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Sensation (सनसनी/अनुभूति): A physical feeling, or a state of intense public interest — unrelated to success/failure.

• Option 2: Opulence (समृद्धि/वैभव): Great wealth or luxuriousness — describes richness, not the opposite of success.

• Option 3: Victory (विजय): Triumph or success in a contest or struggle — this is actually a synonym of success, not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs of "success" tested by SSC: success × defeat, success × failure, success × setback.

• Be careful not to confuse near-synonyms like "victory" and "triumph" with true antonyms in ANTONYM-based questions — SSC often places a synonym as a distractor option.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word in the following sentence.
His eloquent speech always persuades people to work for their betterment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Articulate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Eloquent" means fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing; expressing ideas clearly and effectively. (सुवक्ता/प्रभावशाली वक्ता)
◦ Example: The eloquent lawyer convinced the jury within minutes.

• Its closest synonym among the options is "Articulate", meaning able to express oneself clearly and effectively in speech. (स्पष्टवादी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Vague (अस्पष्ट): Not clearly expressed or defined — nearly the opposite of eloquent.

• Option 2: Inarticulate (अस्पष्ट वक्ता): Unable to express oneself clearly — the direct antonym of "articulate"/"eloquent".

• Option 4: Short (छोटा/संक्षिप्त): Brief in length or duration — unrelated to fluency or persuasiveness of speech.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "eloquent" useful for SSC: "fluent", "expressive", "persuasive", "silver-tongued".

• Related word: "eloquence" (noun) — fluent, persuasive speaking or writing.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. A big fancy dress ball was arranged to celebrate their homecoming.
B. It must have been a terrible shock for a young girl.
C. They had been married a month, just home from their honeymoon.
D. Just as the guests were starting to arrive, Charnley locked himself into his bedroom and shot himself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BCAD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence (B), "It must have been a terrible shock for a young girl," works as the opening line of the paragraph. It is a dramatic, scene-setting statement — a common narrative technique of starting with the emotional impact of an event before explaining what actually happened, so the pronoun "It" refers forward to the shocking incident narrated in the sentences that follow.

• Sentence (C), "They had been married a month, just home from their honeymoon," logically follows (B), as it introduces who "the young girl" is and gives the background — a newly married couple just back from their honeymoon.

• Sentence (A), "A big fancy dress ball was arranged to celebrate their homecoming," follows next, continuing the background by describing the celebration planned for the couple's return.

• Sentence (D), "Just as the guests were starting to arrive, Charnley locked himself into his bedroom and shot himself," comes last, as it reveals the shocking climax — the actual event that (B) referred to at the start.

• Reading the paragraph in this order — B-C-A-D — gives a coherent narrative: the shock is announced first, then the background (marriage, homecoming, the ball) is filled in, and finally the tragic event itself is revealed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: BCDA is incorrect because it places the tragic event (D) before the description of the ball being arranged (A), which disturbs the natural build-up to the climax.

• Option 2: ABCD is incorrect because it opens with the ball being arranged before establishing who "their" refers to, and it separates the opening emotional hook (B) from its natural position.

• Option 4: DACB is incorrect because it reveals the shocking event (D) first without any build-up, and then illogically describes the ball being arranged (A) after Charnley has already shot himself.

NOTE

• In paragraph-jumble questions, look out for an opening line that uses a pronoun ("it", "he", "she", "they") referring forward — this is a common literary device, and such a sentence is not automatically disqualified from being the first sentence.

• Always identify the sentence that introduces names/background (here, sentence C) as it usually anchors the paragraph's context.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
He must deliver pizza.
option_1: Pizza has to be delivered by him.
option_2: Pizza have to be delivered by him.
option_3: Pizza must be delivered by him.
option_4: Pizza can be delivered by him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pizza must be delivered by him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "He must deliver pizza" uses the modal auxiliary "must" in the Active Voice.

• Rule — Passive Voice with Modal Auxiliaries:
◦ Active: Subject + modal + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + modal + be + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "pizza" becomes the subject; the modal "must" is retained as it is (modals do not change form); "deliver" becomes "be delivered"; and "he" becomes the agent "by him".
◦ Passive: Pizza must be delivered by him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has to be delivered" changes the meaning from "must" (obligation) to "has to" (necessity), which is not a faithful modal-for-modal conversion.

• Option 2 is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1, and also because "have to" does not agree with the singular subject "Pizza" in this structure.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "can be delivered" changes the meaning from obligation (must) to ability/possibility (can), which alters the sense of the original sentence.

NOTE

• When converting sentences with modal verbs (must, can, may, should, will, etc.) from active to passive, the modal itself is never changed — only the structure around it changes to "modal + be + V3".

• Other examples: "You should submit the form" → "The form should be submitted by you"; "She can solve this problem" → "This problem can be solved by her."

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
The________(crux) of his argument was that education should continue throughout life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. essence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Crux" means the most important, decisive or central point of a matter. (मूल बिंदु/सार)
◦ Example: The crux of the problem was a lack of communication between the two departments.

• Its closest synonym among the options is "Essence", meaning the intrinsic, most important quality or central point of something. (सार/मूल तत्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Proposal (प्रस्ताव): A plan or suggestion put forward for consideration — not the same as the central point of an argument.

• Option 3: Etiquette (शिष्टाचार): The customary code of polite behaviour — entirely unrelated to the meaning of "crux".

• Option 4: Draft (मसौदा): A preliminary or rough version of a piece of writing — unrelated to "the central point".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "crux" useful for SSC: "gist", "core", "kernel", "nucleus", "heart (of the matter)".

• Do not confuse "crux" (central point) with "critique" (a detailed analysis/review).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
She believed she had been blamed for the mistakes of others for what happened.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Made a scapegoat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "blamed for the mistakes of others" means that a person is unfairly made to bear the blame that actually belongs to someone else.

• The most appropriate substitute is "Made a scapegoat" — a "scapegoat" is a person who is unfairly blamed for the wrongdoings, mistakes or faults of others. (बलि का बकरा बनाना)
◦ Example: After the project failed, the youngest team member was made a scapegoat, though the fault lay with the manager.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Made a sceptic (संशयवादी बनाना): A "sceptic" is a person who doubts generally accepted beliefs — unrelated to being unfairly blamed.

• Option 3: Made a spinster (अविवाहित स्त्री): A "spinster" is an older unmarried woman — entirely unrelated to blame.

• Option 4: Made a savage (क्रूर व्यक्ति बनाना): A "savage" is a fierce, uncivilised or brutal person — unrelated to the given meaning.

NOTE

• Related idiom: "To scapegoat someone" (verb) means to unfairly blame someone for something that is not their fault.

• Other useful one-word substitutes on blame/fault: "culprit" (a person who has committed an offence), "instigator" (one who incites wrongdoing).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Nobody’s fool
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Not easily deceived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Nobody's fool" means a person who is sensible, shrewd and not easily deceived, tricked or fooled by others. (चालाक/जिसे आसानी से मूर्ख नहीं बनाया जा सकता)
◦ Example: Be careful trying to trick her — she is nobody's fool.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: The wisest person — this overstates the meaning; the idiom implies shrewdness in not being deceived, not being the wisest person overall.

• Option 3: A complete fool — this is the literal opposite of the intended idiomatic meaning.

• Option 4: All are fools — this misreads "nobody's" as if it meant "everybody", which is incorrect.

NOTE

• Other idioms built on foolishness often asked in SSC: "No fool like an old fool" (an older, experienced person acting foolishly is especially foolish), "Play the fool" (to act in a silly, joking manner).

• Do not confuse "Nobody's fool" with "Fool's paradise" (a state of happiness based on false belief or hope).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They secret.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the segment "They secret". As used here, "secret" is meant to modify the verb "decided", but an adjective cannot modify a verb — only an adverb can.

• Rule — Adverbs modify verbs: To describe the manner in which an action is performed (here, the manner of deciding), an adverb must be used, not an adjective. The adjective "secret" must therefore be changed to the adverb "secretly".
◦ Correct sentence: They secretly decided to leave the town.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "decided" is grammatically correct; it is the correct past tense form of the verb "decide".

• Option 3: "the town" is grammatically correct; it is a correctly formed noun phrase acting as the object of "to leave".

• Option 4: "to leave" is grammatically correct; it is the correct infinitive form following the verb "decided" (decided + to + V1).

NOTE

• Adjectives generally end in forms like "-ful", "-ous", "-ive", "-al", while their corresponding adverbs are usually formed by adding "-ly" (secret → secretly, quiet → quietly, careful → carefully).

• Always check whether a describing word in a sentence is modifying a noun (needs an adjective) or a verb/adjective/another adverb (needs an adverb) — this is one of the most common SSC error-spotting traps.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "It has come as a surprise __ Scheduled Tribes..." The fixed phrase in English is "to come as a surprise to (someone)", meaning something is unexpected from that person's point of view.

• Rule — Fixed Preposition: The idiomatic expression "a surprise to somebody" always takes the preposition "to", not "off", "in" or "at".
◦ Example: His resignation came as a surprise to everyone in the office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "off" does not fit; "surprise off" is not a valid English collocation.

• Option 2: "in" does not fit; "surprise in" does not correctly follow the fixed phrase "come as a surprise".

• Option 4: "at" does not fit here; while "surprised at (something)" is valid, the fixed phrase "come as a surprise" specifically takes "to", not "at".

NOTE

• Other common prepositional phrases with "surprise": "to my surprise", "surprised at/by (an event)", "take someone by surprise".

• Always memorise such fixed preposition + noun/adjective combinations, as they are frequently tested in SSC cloze passages.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. among.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Scheduled Tribes who are __ the most marginalised groups of the country." The intended meaning is that Scheduled Tribes are counted as part of a larger group (the most marginalised groups), which requires the preposition "among".

• Rule — "Among" for inclusion in a group: "Among" is used to show that someone/something is included as one of a group of three or more people/things.
◦ Example: She is among the finest singers of her generation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "through" does not fit; it indicates movement or means, not inclusion in a group.

• Option 2: "therefore" does not fit grammatically at all in this position, as it is a conjunction/adverb of result, not a preposition that can sit between "are" and "the most marginalised groups".

• Option 3: "onto" does not fit; it indicates movement to a position on a surface, unrelated to the intended meaning here.

NOTE

• Distinguish "among" (used for three or more) from "between" (used for exactly two).

• Other common uses: "divide among the three of them", "choose among several options".

Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. marginalised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "The Adivasis of India have been __ socially, economically and culturally." The passage as a whole discusses the Adivasis (Scheduled Tribes) being one of the most disadvantaged groups, so the word must continue this sense of being pushed to the margins of society.

• "Marginalised" means treated as insignificant or peripheral; pushed to the edge of social, economic or cultural life, which fits perfectly with "socially, economically and culturally" that follows it.
◦ Example: Marginalised communities often lack access to quality education and healthcare.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "censored" means officially suppressed or examined for objectionable content — unrelated to a community's social/economic condition.

• Option 3: "elevated" means raised to a higher position or level — this contradicts the passage's overall tone of describing disadvantage and suffering.

• Option 4: "uplifted" means raised in status or condition — this also contradicts the negative context, since the passage separately addresses this positive idea in blank 5, describing what has NOT yet fully happened.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the surrounding sentences (not just the sentence containing the blank) to catch the overall tone of the passage — here, the tone is clearly about disadvantage ("despite various efforts...still under poverty and suffering"), which rules out "elevated"/"uplifted" for blank 3.

• Related words: "marginalisation" (noun), "underprivileged", "disadvantaged", "downtrodden".

Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. poverty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under __ and suffering." The phrase "under poverty and suffering" fits the passage's context of describing the continued hardship faced by marginalised communities.

• "Poverty" means the state of being extremely poor; lacking sufficient money or means, which logically pairs with "suffering" in describing the community's condition.
◦ Example: Millions of people around the world still live under poverty despite economic growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "abundance" means a very large quantity of something — this contradicts the context of continued hardship despite government efforts.

• Option 2: "forest" is a geographical term with no logical connection to "and suffering" in this sentence.

• Option 3: "river" is also a geographical term, unrelated to the described social condition.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "poverty" useful for SSC cloze passages: "live in/under poverty", "poverty-stricken", "poverty alleviation", "below the poverty line".

• In cloze questions, always check that the chosen word logically pairs with the word joined to it by "and" or "or" — here, the blank must pair sensibly with "suffering".

Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. elevation of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Therefore, the __ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted." The sentence is discussing the act of raising/promoting a leader from a marginalised community to a high position (such as the Presidency mentioned at the start of the passage).

• "Elevation of" means the act of raising someone to a higher rank, position or status, which correctly completes the sense — "the elevation of a leader...to a high position does not automatically mean the whole community has been uplifted."
◦ Example: The elevation of a woman to the post of CEO was seen as a landmark moment for the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "rejection of" means the refusal to accept someone — this contradicts the passage, which is about a leader being placed in a high position (as President), not rejected.

• Option 2: "president of" is grammatically and logically incorrect here, as it does not fit the sentence structure "the ___ a leader..." — a leader cannot be "the president of a leader".

• Option 3: "exclusion of" means leaving someone out or shutting them out — again the opposite of what the passage describes (the leader being placed in a prominent position).

NOTE

• Related words: "elevate" (verb) — to raise in rank, position, or status; "elevation" (noun) — very commonly used in passages discussing promotions or appointments to high office.

• In cloze passages about social/political upliftment, watch for near-opposite distractor options (like "rejection"/"exclusion" here) placed alongside the correct word ("elevation") to test careful reading of context.
